utterances.text: Okay. If we could go to page 2 of your annex, and I'll tell you the page in e-court. I believe it's page 8 in e-court, in the English, and page 10 in the B/C/S, I think. Yes, that's right.

utterances.text: Okay. And now with respect to the Cancari Road graves, is there any new information in your report as concerns these graves, versus your old report, or your more recent report, I should say?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, there was a -- there was a change in relation to which of the Cancari secondary graves are related to the primary graves Kozluk and Branjevo. So from our previous investigations, we know that bodies from primary graves Kozluk and Branjevo were reburied to along the Cancari Road graves. These secondary graves were found by the ICTY, 12 of them, and additional one, the 13 one, by the BiH authorities. So we have in total 13 secondary graves along this road. And in my previous report, I linked Cancari Road 5 and 4, as well as 6. But at that time we didn't have any identifications yet from this Cancari Road 6 secondary grave. I linked these sites to Kozluk, and that was based on the green glass which was found -- which was found inside these graves. Previously, we referred as being green glass linked to Kozluk grave, where a lot of green glass was found inside this primary grave, and also in related Cancari Road 3 grave which was exhumed by the ICTY, it was confirmed, but through forensic evidence, that this secondary grave is related to Kozluk. So based on the green glass which was found in the site Cancari Road 4, 5, and 6, we have linked -- I have linked these secondary graves to Kozluk primary site. But when we received the update of the ICMP data in February of 2010, there we have already new identifications -- or first identifications and additional identifications from Cancari Road 4 and 6. And based on the DNA connections, I found out that these graves are not connected to Branjevo, but to -- are not connected to Kozluk primary grave, but rather to Branjevo grave-site. So we'll see, when we will go over the DNA connection portion of my report, how many connections -- DNA connections have been established between these graves, and you will see on the charts why I considered these graves -- these secondary graves being related to Branjevo grave and not to Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just ask you a few questions about this. You say that the attribution of these graves or the association of these graves with Kozluk was based upon the finding of green glass?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in relation to the other Cancari graves where green glass was found, was there an indication as to how much green glass was found?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We have an example for Cancari Road 1, which was exhumed last year, and I also attend this site for two days, and you can find in the ICMP report that it -- a lot of green glass have been found, a huge amount over all the deposits inside the grave. So they have made this distinction between small amount and huge amount of green glass.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is there any indication in the ICMP summary reports that you reviewed in relation to Cancari Road 4 and 6, whether that's the same green glass that was found in the other Cancari graves, same type of green glass?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no indication on that, if that is -- if that is the same type, or any other evidence on it, nor we have any scientific report about this types of the glass. It's just the matter that there is a green glass. And besides that, it's not only green glass inside these Cancari 4 and 6; it's also another type of -- types of glass have been found.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How does this impact your prior and this new report concerning the number of Kozluk-related graves -- or individuals, I should say, and the Branjevo-related individuals?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, it impacts on the total number of the individuals found in -- or individuals which can be attributed to the particular primary grave and subsequently to execution point. So the number for Kozluk -- the total number for Kozluk-related victims is now significantly lower; for, I think, more than 200 individuals. And for Branjevo-related individuals, it's higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is it substantially higher or slightly higher? Do you know? Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same -- the same number of individuals, which are less for Kozluk site, are now added to Branjevo site --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janc, what can you tell us about this Bljeceva 1 grave?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bljeceva 1 grave is a significant one because it is a mixed grave, and this is the only mixed grave related to the secondary and primary graves which are discussed in my report. When I say "mixed grave," I mean that inside this grave are the individuals which are related to the Srebrenica events and also on the individuals which are related to some other events; in particular, events in Bratunac in May of 1992. So inside this grave, there were individuals disposed from two different events, and most of the individuals inside this grave is not related to Srebrenica events. So far, we have 49 identifications related to Srebrenica, and I think a little bit more than 90 individuals have been identified in relation to other event.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in relation to the Bljeceva 1 grave, how did you count the number of individuals, in terms of your report? Did you count all of the individuals in the grave, or did you only count some of them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just counted the one which are -- which are related to Srebrenica, which are victims of the Srebrenica -- on the missing list -- on the Srebrenica missing list. I just counted those individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How did you make the association between the people that were -- well, how did you make the connection between the people that were found there that were associated with Srebrenica, versus the people that were found there that were not associated with Srebrenica? How was that determined?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who are related to Srebrenica, their names appear on the ICMP missing list and also on the -- actually, not on the ICMP, but the ICRC missing list. So they went missing after the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how were you able to determine the individuals that weren't from Srebrenica, what event, if any, they were related to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We also received the ICMP data on the identified individuals which are related to other events, and in the relation to that I consulted our Demographic Unit, who prepared a list of the individuals which are from the other events and found inside these graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So for the people that are non-Srebrenica-related, was that determined on the basis of their identity as is found in other records?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was that determined on the basis of DNA identification or matching?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, again correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does this mixing of individuals from separate events occur with respect to the Bljeceva 2 grave?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is only in respect to Bljeceva 1 grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in respect of your review of the individuals found in these graves, did you review ICMP summary reports concerning them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, and the fact that they -- they found -- the individuals from two different events was spotted during the exhumation by them.

utterances.text: Yes. This is summary report for Bljeceva 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janc, can you -- first of all, do you know whether or not there are any other graves that concern your analysis that are mixed, besides the Bljeceva 1 grave?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there are no -- there is no such graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how can you rule out that possibility?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is based on the findings during the exhumations, and especially I reviewed all the summary reports for all the graves from the ICMP, and they haven't spotted any such -- such instances with the other graves. There was, I can mention, for example, for Zeleni Jadar 2, when they exhumed that grave, it was already established before by the ICTY -- Professor Richard Wright was there, and he established that this secondary grave was robbed. So some bodies were taken out of secondary grave and buried somewhere else. We still don't know where. We don't have -- this location of this tertiary grave which is related to the Zeleni Jadar 2 is not known to the ICTY yet. And also during that exhumation, because that grave was exhumed by the BiH authorities in 2008, I think, or 2007, they have spotted the same issue, the same fact, that this grave was robbed. So -- and that's why I'm saying that the ICMP archaeologists are very precise in their determination, if these graves are mixed, robbed, and what was going on with the graves. And when I -- when I don't see any indication in their reports that the graves might be mixed, or any other indications, I can exclude the possibility that these are mixed -- the other graves are also mixed graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to the determination of the fact that the Bljeceva 1 grave is mixed, is that new to your report, or new in your report, I should say?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not new. This fact was already known to the ICTY before, and it was already in Dean Manning's report and also in my last report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you're referring to Dean Manning's report in 2007?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Dean Manning's report from 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And it was discussed in your previous report, you've said?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, also it was discussed in my previous report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to go to -- back, I should say, to 5754A, which is annex A. I meant 25 in the English. I'm sorry. If we can just go to the next page in the English, so ERN ending 997. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE

utterances.text: Now, with respect to this grave, you'd indicated that it had been robbed. Can you tell us what that means.

utterances.text: I think I already explained that the bodies were taken out from this secondary grave and buried -- reburied again into so far unknown tertiary grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If I could just have in e-court, please, 65 ter 6265.

utterances.text: Okay. And what's that based on?

utterances.text: It's based on -- again, on the DNA identifications by the ICMP.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to 65 ter 6265, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]

And this grave is actually located, I would say, around four kilometres away from the Rogatica centre town.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And based on your investigation and your involvement in this matter, can you tell us a little bit about who each of these individuals are? Let's start with Avdo Palic.

And we have some information and witness statement of his movement after his capture on twenty - I think - seven of July, 1995. Later on, he was taken to the Borika Hotel, from there to -- somewhere to Rogatica, where he was kept in an apartment and interrogated by the members of the security branch of the VRS Main Staff. And after that, he was taken to Bijeljina, to Vaniko [phoen] Prison, where he was kept by the members of the IBK Corps.

So there is information that he was taken back towards Han Pijesak at the same night, but after that there is no information about him. And the only information we have now, that he was found in the same grave as the other two Muslim leaders, Mehmed Hajric and Amir Imamovic, and those two were civilian representatives in Zepa. One of them was hodja, I think. The other one, I cannot remember. But both of them were also arrested after the fall of Zepa by the members of the VRS, and those two individuals were then kept and imprisoned in Rasadnik prison in Rogatica for several days or several weeks. And then, according to information to the witnesses which we interviewed, they were taken out of the prison and never seen again. So that was around middle of August, end of August, somewhere at that time. And also these two individuals are found, as we can see, together with Avdo Palic, in the same grave.

utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you have a designation here "Others"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I briefly testified about it already yesterday. Those others are designated for four different categories of the sites. utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me ask you a little bit about the Serbia-related individuals. Has your investigation -- can your investigation explain how that came to be, that there were Srebrenica-related bodies recovered in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There can be several different reasons for that, but the closest one will be because we know that Kozluk execution point was just next to the Drina River, and I think we have statements of some of the individuals and -- that there were cases where people fled from the execution point and tried to cross the Drina River. So that would be one reason why certain people were shot while trying to escape over the Drina River on the Serbian territory, and then they were just found a few kilometres down in Serbia in the same river.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go to the following page in English, ending ERN 6009, and I believe the following page in the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And here you have a reference to surface remains, particularly in Kozluk and Godinjske Bare. And I would ask you if you could explain to the Trial Chamber why you've considered these surface remains separately from the surface remains that are documented in annex B to your report. Let's start with Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yesterday, I said that for Kozluk, it is difficult to distinguish if those bodies were, indeed, just left on the surface or they were initially buried. And after several years, when they were exposed to different weather condition and due to natural causes, were just found on the surface then, so that's why. And an additional reason why I placed them here, they're out of the route where the column was moving towards Nezuk, and they are very close to the execution point. So, as such, it would be very unlikely that those bodies would be found there and would be, I would say, combat casualties, so that's why I am placing them here as "Others," because, indeed, I cannot clearly say if they were part of this execution which was done at Kozluk site. So next, the second one are Godinjske Bare individuals. Those are related to the six individuals which were killed in Trnovo, and they were -- this execution was actually filmed. And we know they are not casualties of any combat, that they are casualties of the crime, and that's why I place them here. Although found on the surface, we know what was the fate of these individuals and how, actually, they were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are there any other -- any other surface remains that you considered as victims of murder?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, there is. There is one individual for which we know was executed and is found on the surface, and, as such, is part of my surface remains section. So there is an individual found in Tisova Kosa, I think, and the individual was named by the Nezuk survivor who was executed at that point at time -- in time together with him. So he pointed at that individual, along with the others, and he was found on the surface; not only him, but also the others, but we don't know the other names which are around -- which were found around this individual named by the Nezuk survivor, were not identified by this Nezuk survivor. So it's only one individual who was there. And also by this Nezuk survivor, there is another individual mentioned who was then found in Brezljak grave, taken away from that spot and mentioned -- and found in Brezljak grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the Court's -- for the record, the Nezuk survivor that the witness is referring to is the subject of a pending 92 bis application as PW-0001 -- 009, 009.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: A question from Judge Mindua.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, while the Prosecutor is putting his house in order, I have a short question for you. I'm concerned about these surface remains. I had already put this question to one of the witnesses that came before us. I wanted to know what the cause for death would be in that instance, and the witness had said that it was most probably due to combat, the person was killed in combat, because the person would have -- the people who were executed had actually been buried. But in light of the explanation you have provided, you are saying that among the surface remains that you found, there would probably be the remains of people who had been executed. My question, therefore, is to know whether you conducted any analysis or whether you used any methods to mark a distinction between those remains you found on the surface and those people who had been executed, on the one hand, and those persons who would have died in combat. Do you have a way of establishing a difference between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's -- it's not easy to distinguish between the two, especially for those which are found on a surface. The best way we have right now is to check the witness statements, as it was with this one with the Nezuk survivor, where he identified several other individuals being shot together with him and now they are found on the surface. For such individuals, we can certainly say, yes, they are not -- they are not -- they are not killed in combat, but they are executed, they are part of the crime. On the other hand, for -- for establishing, for example, the cause of death and everything, we would need every -- for every single person found on the surface, we would need the autopsy records and all the other documentation. That one we don't have for every single individual. And since the surface remains were never that -- part of this Srebrenica investigation, we were always more interested in what is found in the grave. I can say that we don't have, for every single individual -- or that we have for only a minority of these individuals found on the surface, that we have documentation on them. But regardless of that, we have witness statements and documents which are referring to combat activities in the area of where the column was passing, and based on those we can see -- we can say that most -- most probably most of those found on the surface were casualties of the combats. On the other hand, we also have instances where we have that some of them committed suicides during this breakthrough, then some of them were just casualties of the minefields, and, as we can see now, based on the witness statements, some of them were executed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. That is extremely clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could go to P170, and I believe it's page 37 in English -- no, 39 in English, and it should be page 55 -- yeah, it will be 55 and 56 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, in this part of your report, you've indicated "Uncategorised Sites," and if you could just explain, very briefly, what that is. I think you covered some of that your answer to Judge Mindua's question, but if you could tell us basically what this chart shows and what it means.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are 38 individuals which were found in different locations. And while requesting for documentation on these particular sites, we haven't received -- or the documentation we received was insufficient to conclude if they were found on the surface or were found in graves. They are Srebrenica-related victims, because they are on a missing list, but we cannot say if they were found in the graves or on the surface. That's why I separated them from other countings.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in relation to what you've related to us concerning the Nezuk surface remains, can you tell us anything in relation to the Snagovo graves?

utterances.text: Can we go to P170, page 38 in English. It will be 55 in B/C/S. All right, I've misspoken again. Not 38; it will be 40. Okay. I think we have to go to the bottom of the page to find it in B/C/S. It's 57 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this chart shows, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This chart shows the number -- the total number of identified individuals per certain execution site. So I've put together the numbers we can see at the beginning of my report for particular execution site. For example, here we can see, for Kravica and others, so we know that execution site at Kravica, that the bodies were removed to Glogova primary grave and Drnica [phoen] primary grave, and that at Glogova site also the other bodies were buried. So the bodies which were picked up in Bratunac, then along the Konjevic -- some of the bodies along the Konjevic Polje road, and some of the individuals which were captured by Serbian authorities and returned back to Bosnia authorities from 20th of July onwards. So those bodies are also there. That's why we cannot distinguish how many of them have been, indeed, taken from Kravica execution point. But based on the information we have for the other sites, based on the witness statements, witness testimony, we can conclude that most of them are for sure taken from Kravica. So most of the totals, 1.334 individuals which were found in Glogova and Kravica-related primary and secondary graves must have been executed at Kravica, because there is not many of the individuals -- I would say around 300, maximum 400, which were taken from the other sites, Bratunac, along the road, and from the other incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you have any forensic -- that is, non-DNA-related information concerning establishing a connection between Kravica, Glogova, and any associated graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we have also other evidence which links these secondary and primary graves, and we'll see what kind of evidence we have when we'll be going over my charts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we could just go to the next page, I think, in both documents. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here we see, at the bottom, it says "All sites total," the number is "5390." That's different than the number 5777 that you've indicated in the main section of your report. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber why that is different?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I include it here and counted only the numbers where we have primary and related secondary graves, and these are the biggest execution sites. And I did not count into these totals the sites where we have primary undisturbed graves: For example, here we don't have the Cerska execution -- Cerska mass grave, Bisina, Mrsici, and other graves. So what I counted here, so what you can see here, all sites total, this is related to the sites you can see in this table only. So -- and you can see, for example, breaking down totals for particular execution sites, as this Orahovac we have 830; Petkovci, 809; Kozluk, 761; and Branjevo-Pilica, 1656, which in a way shows us a pattern that around 800 people have been executed at certain execution point, although we have to be careful with that because we don't have -- not all the individuals have been identified yet from these execution sites. Especially, we are still waiting some identifications to be made from Cancari 1 and Cancari 8, which were exhumed and not counted yet for this, but we will have roughly these numbers as they are here. They will be growing for each of these sites, but around 800 people per execution site.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want to focus you, if I can, on the totals that you've indicated here for Kozluk and for Branjevo in this report. It appears you've indicated that the total Kozluk-related graves is 761. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And then for Branjevo-Pilica-related graves, 1656?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to the Branjevo and Pilica graves, is that number more or less consistent with the evidence that the investigation has revealed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can say -- I can confirm that, because in Branjevo Military Farm grave-site we have the bodies which were executed at Branjevo and also the bodies which were taken from Pilica Cultural Dom and taken to this primary grave. So -- and based on the investigation and witness statements and everything, we can conclude that this is quite -- quite exact number, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But, again, that's different than the number that you had indicated in relation to your report from 2009, right, March 2009?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, because, I mean, March 2009, Cancari Road 5 was -- Cancari Road 4 and 5, as well as 6, were attached to the Kozluk execution point.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And so the totals that you had at that point in March 2009 were 960 for Branjevo -- is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that must be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And 1.040 for Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to move into your section concerning the surface remains as annex B to your report. It should be, really, just the next page. Okay. And the following page, we can see the text. It should be the same also in the B/C/S. And we've talked a bit about surface remains. Can you just tell us how this section of your report is organised, in brief terms. And, in particular, if you could focus on these four categories that are indicated in the fourth paragraph of the report. It will have to be the next page for the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First we have a brief summary of how I -- how I have analysed these data. Based on which information I have received from different sources, I have came up with the total numbers of the individuals found on the surface. Those individuals will all appear -- and all appears on the ICMP identification list, also, along with the individuals which are found in the graves. So in order -- in order to distinguish them, you have to know what particular site code has been attached to these surface remains. And when you find that a particular site code was attached to a certain site, and that surface remains were collected, then you know that you can attach these individuals found on the surface, and if they are Srebrenica-related victims, inside certain areas. And for Srebrenica, because I distinguished between Srebrenica-related surface remains and then we have also Zepa-related surface remains, which were not part of my previous report, we have 15 individuals from Zepa, but -- so the others -- the others, 688, are related to Srebrenica. And I have categorised these surface remains into four areas, as you can see here. The Pobudje area, which is stretching south of the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, then the Baljkovica area, the Snagovo area, which are all the area which are on the route where the column was passing in 1995 -- July 1995. And then I have other areas here. These are the areas which are outside of the above-mentioned area but are relatively close, still close to these areas. We will have a map showing of where these surface remains were actually found. And if you go to the next page, we'll see how many of those individuals were found in certain areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let's take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is the one. And for Pobudje area, you can see here that the most -- the most individuals have been found there, so along -- in the woods along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road. So it is in the area leading down from Buljim up to Konjevic Polje area. So in this area, the most of them have been collected from the ground and so far identified. We have almost -- it is 558 individuals so far identified in that area. Then next area would be Baljkovica, where we have 66 of them identified. So this is the second-largest area, and we know that there were -- there was fighting going on and a breakthrough of the Muslim column, and this is not surprising me, that we have -- we have surface remains there. And also then we have a few of them -- I would say 16 of them in Snagovo area, which is south of Zvornik, I would say between those two areas we have been discussing before, between Pobudje and Baljkovica area, so in the area between those two. And then we have other -- other areas, where we have 48 individuals so far identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I just want to show you a map, and if you could relate that to the areas that you've just indicated. It's 65 ter 5416. And we'll have to go -- I'd like to go, actually, first to the last page. I think it's page 23. Yes, that's right. And I'd like to have the witness mark this map, please, just so you can indicate for the Trial Chamber where the respective areas are that you're referring to, Pobudje, Baljkovica, Snagovo, and the other areas you've indicated.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, I would like to say that we received this map from the BiH Commission on Missing Persons, and based on their data they provided on these surface remains, they have also created this map for us in order to present geographically where these bodies are located. So -- and I can mark -- I can mark the areas which I am referring in my report. And I have to emphasise, before I mark, that not all the individuals we can see on this map have been identified already. So -- but the concentration of these individuals would be -- would be the same, regardless of if they were identified yet or not. So I would first mark the area of Pobudje.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if you could designate that "P" so that we know how to find it.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] This is the area where we have the highest concentration of the identifications and surface remains. Then the second area is Snagovo area [marks]. I will mark it as S. And then we have Baljkovica area. I'll mark it as B [marks]. And then we have other areas, so I can just mark few of them that you can have -- I will mark them as O [marks], and this O [marks], and this O [marks], also this one down there, O [marks]. Yeah, and these are the other areas. So they are -- if you can see here that the areas from Pobudje up to the north, towards Baljkovica, is the area where the column was passing. All the other areas are relatively close to these areas, but not on the exact route. But we know that people were running different directions, so the large quantity of people were moving towards Nezuk, but some of them were just fleeing another direction. So it's not surprising me to find some other individuals in the other areas also.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I just want to show you -- yes. I'd like to have this admitted, Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This map with the markings will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P206.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And then I'd like to have the witness shown the page just previous to this and have him mark that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what I'd like you to indicate for the Trial Chamber is the direction of the column as the investigation has revealed it to be.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, no problem. So the direction of the column is going from here [marks]. It crosses the road here [marks]. So then it goes up towards the north and crosses the road again here [marks], and towards Nezuk. So this is the route of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if you would, could you write "Nezuk" at the top of your arrow so we know what direction that's intended to point.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right, thank you for that. I'd like to tender this marked map as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received. And Judge Nyambe has a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First the number, please, exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P207.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. I just need your help to understand your submission with regard to the Srebrenica surface remains. On the previous document, you said something to the effect that the locations where some correlated surface remains have been collected, they were consistent with the route of the Muslim column; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay. The surface remains, therefore, on this route, can you tell or are you able to say how they died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that for most of them, as I explained before, we can say they are combat casualties. But for some of them, we know from witness statements and other information we have, that they have died -- they committed suicide or died when passing the minefields, and some of them were killed, executed. And as I also said, we don't have these autopsy reports, all of them, here in house. Certainly, we can request them and try to find additional indication of how they died, but I'm quite concerned that we'll get any specific results on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And has the investigation given you any indication as to how these particular individuals basically got from Srebrenica to Trnovo, the circumstances under which -- under which they got there? Do you have any indication as to had?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see from the video, they were -- they were there, executed by the members of the Serb paramilitary forces, I think. So that's how they have made it there. I cannot remember from the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And now I'd like to go to a different area of your evidence, and that concerns annex C of your report. utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Annex C is related to DNA connections which have been established based on the ICMP data we have been provided with between the primary graves -- primary/secondary graves and secondary graves, itself. So when analysing the ICMP data, we have found several individuals which were found in two different graves, some of them even in three different graves. And in case -- to establish a DNA connection, what this term actually means, it is one DNA connection of the individual found in two different graves. So if one -- if body parts of one individuals -- of one individual were found in two different graves, that would mean one connection. And as you can see in my table, there are different numbers. And when I say number of DNA connection cases, I would say one case means that one individual was found in two different graves. And you can see different colours inside my table under "DNA Connections," "Connection Between" column, and those relates -- when you see in green, it means there is a DNA connection established between a primary and a secondary grave. And those in blue represent the DNA connection between the secondary graves, itself. So then the number of established connections, you can see under the last column. So we'll have two different colours on the second page. One would be the actual -- related to the connections between the disturbed primary graves, itself, and the last one would be the connection established between the execution point, in that case Kravica execution point, and secondary mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could go briefly to page 50 in the English, and I believe it will be -- it should be three pages up in the B/C/S, and that should be 67 -- or 68, 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Are you able to tell us -- well, we can see, actually, the three different colours or so represented in certain totals here, and you've indicated six primary-to-primary DNA connections; 265 primary-to-secondary DNA connections; 407 secondary-to-secondary DNA connections; and 1, it says, total execution site secondary graves. For a total of 679 DNA connections; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, I was able to establish 679 connections in total when analysing the ICMP data. And we have been talking about the methodology, how it was done, when I was testifying about the sample page 7 and 6 before, so how it was done with the actual ICMP data that I analysed in order to get to a conclusion of total cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First, let me ask you -- if we can go to the following page for both documents. This is an index part of annex C. And in terms of counting these DNA connections, can you just illustrate for the Trial Chamber how did you that. I'm going to refer to you a particular line, if we can get it big enough to see, and it should be midway down -- midway down the page, it's "7322-06." You'll see that in the far left column, "Protocol ID." It's right in the middle, and it indicates Bljeceva 1, Bljeceva 2 - do you see that, Mr. Janc - and then there is a series of entries under the case ID. There are one, two, three, four, five, six entries.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can explain. And before that I do that, I would like to just explain one more thing. When I said that certain individual -- body parts of certain individuals were found in even three graves, those connections would be counted as three connections, which is between grave-site A and B, B and C, and A and C. So although they are related to only one individual which was found in three different graves, there would be -- this individual would be counted -- not individual, but rather the connection would be counted three times, because we have -- actually, we have three connections. So -- but I think I have -- we have around 30 or 40 of such individuals, so the total number of 676 connections are related to six hundred - I think - eighteen individuals. And let me comment on this now. Yes, here we can see this is a reorganised chart when we have made and concluded the analysis of the chart of the ICMP data. So we have reorganised it in order to present it to the Trial Chamber and to easier -- for easier understanding. As you can see, the first column, there is a protocol ID, and what I have been already discussing, the protocol ID is the most important indicator or the most important information inside the ICMP data about the unique DNA profile, that it refers to one individual. So that's what we have been looking for. And if we found this protocol ID in two different graves, actually, that body -- body parts were found in two different graves and then attached to the same protocol ID, it means that one individual was found in two different graves. And here we can see site number 1, it refers -- and site number 2, it refers easily to the grave-sites, and we can see for this particular individual that body parts were found in Bljeceva 1 and Bljeceva 2 secondary graves. And then if we move to the columns right, where it says at the top "Case IDs of the same protocol ID," so we have been able to find, in this ICMP data, that many case IDs for this particular protocol ID. So it means here, for Bljeceva 1, one body part of this individual was found in Bljeceva 1 secondary grave. The other five body parts were identified in Bljeceva 2 graves -- secondary graves. And regardless of this fact that we have so many body parts found, this individual would be counted only as one connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Off the top of your head, what's the -- what's the largest number of graves that you've been able to match to any one given individual?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]

utterances.text: Now, you've also dealt with somewhat unusual cases concerning your DNA connections?

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit about that?

Because Glogova 5 is in the area south, and Kozluk and Cancari also are in the area north, and based on the evidence we have so far about the connection between the graves, it would be -- this connection would be very unusual, because we don't have any confirmation that Glogova-related graves are connected somehow to Cancari graves. So the same would be for several other cases. We can see here, for example, the first entry, here we have a different situation. The first entry, it is the connection, DNA connection, established between Cerska and Hodzici 2 and 3. We know that Cerska grave is a primary grave, not disturbed one, and it would be very unusual that there would be a connection. And when I have been looking into this particular case, I have found out that there have been twins which were identified -- which one of them was identified under the same protocol ID. And my conclusion would be that there is an actual problem, because I know that when you have twins, the twins have the unique DNA profile, and in that case I would say it's most probably that one of the bodies was found in Cerska 2, the other brother was found in Hodzici Road. And because they cannot distinguish between the DNA samples, there is a match now in ICMP records. So -- and for these cases which were unusual to us, we have sent -- and I also reviewed the autopsy records, and for some of those cases I found that same pieces of bodies were tested and found as being one -- part of one individual, which is impossible, and that's why we have sent the information to the ICMP in order to get the clarification from their side what would that -- what would that be.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]

utterances.text: And I would like to have P170 shown to the witness again. And I think we were on page 91 in the B/C/S and page 76 in the English, but I'd like to go forward just a page or two. utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]

For Cancari Road 8, we don't have any identifications yet, but what I was able to identify was the ID number of one individual found in the Cancari Road 8 secondary grave. The body parts of this same individual were already before identified at Branjevo -- at Branjevo primary grave, so that's why I can link this Cancari Road 8 grave to a primary Branjevo grave. So then at the bottom, far left at the bottom, you can see the total number of the cases. So it means for Branjevo-related graves, secondary and primary, there is 172 connections -- DNA connections on this chart in total. So that's why I was telling that we can -- we can say, with a great level of certainty, that these graves are, indeed, connected to Branjevo Military Farm. The same is to Kozluk site. And at the bottom, we can see one case which goes between Cancari Road 11 and Cancari Road 7, so it means it goes to unrelated secondary graves. So it is not that impossible that we have a connection -- one DNA connection between these site, because we know that those sites were reburied at rather same period of time. Most probably, the same transport means were used, and it might be that there was a contamination case, so that some body parts remained on the truck and then were just -- when they were loaded with the bodies from another primary graves, were just disposed into the -- into another secondary grave. So -- but if there is one case only, that's not that strong connection. And it might be also that there is a possible different -- there is a kind of different reason for that, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to show you 65 ter 6271. It should be a map. And while that's loading, I noticed you mentioned something about possible contamination through the same -- through the use of the same transportation methods in order to rebury, exhume -- exhume and rebury these individuals from these graves. And I wonder if you might describe, in as brief terms as possible, the types of vehicles, machines that were involved in the exhumation and reburial of these bodies from mass graves -- from primary graves to secondary graves. What kinds of vehicles were involved in those?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of there -- there were trucks and lorries involved in the transportation of the bodies, and the front loaders, I think, for the excavation of the actual bodies from the primary graves and also for preparing the secondary graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you have any information as to how extensive the -- how extensive the damage was to the bodies done by the equipment that was used to bury and rebury, from your review of the forensic information in this case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because these heavy machines were used, so the bodies were extremely damaged when taken from the primary graves and then transported to the secondary graves. And also at the secondary graves, they were dumped into the grave, and then again with heavy machine levelled back and back-filled. So they were damaged, yeah, very damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And they were broken into pieces?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As we can see from all these data from -- forensic data and DNA data, they were in several pieces, and that's why we have so many re-associations in ICMP data.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to focus you on is the top part of this map. If we could move -- maybe the part where it says "RS" to the bottom of the map, as a beginning point, and then we can focus on the top half and then the bottom half, so you can explain to the Trial Chamber what this represents.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this map represents -- I created and based -- and used the base map number 8, what I have been testifying before. And then we created the map in order to graphically represent where those primary and all the secondary graves are. And the red dots -- the bigger red dots represent the primary execution -- primary grave-sites. Then the black dots represent the execution sites. Then we have the green dots, which represent the secondary mass graves. And then we have some smaller red dots, which also represent the graves. So here you can see the actual position of all of the graves, except the individual ones are not on this one. But all the others are here which are part of my report, so that you have idea where those are in relation to the area. So then we have certain arrows, and these arrows represent the movement of the bodies. So based on the evidence I have been presenting here today and we are referring to in our case, we are concluding to which secondary graves bodies were taken from primary graves. And you can see certain circles around the Cancari Road graves, the green ones, so it is just to put them together, which are related to which, from which primary grave to which secondary grave these bodies were taken. So, for example, for the Kozluk site, we have number 1, 2, 3, 13, and then number 7. All the others are related to Branjevo site.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that similarly represented on the southern part of this map, if we could go down and show that for a moment?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, it is similar, and we can see the huge concentration of the execution -- of primary graves in the Konjevic Polje area. Then we have the Kravica warehouse execution point, and, of course, the arrows which goes -- which goes down to secondary graves to represent the movement of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender this map into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janc, I'd like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P212.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, I'd like to ask you, in relation to the movement and the relationship between the primary and secondary mass grave or graves that you have examined in your report, have you had an opportunity to review or examine some of the testimony of survivors in this case; in particular, the Branjevo Farm survivor, the Petkovci Dam survivor, and the Orahovac survivor?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I did; also their statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you able to locate any of the individuals that they have testified to as having been at these execution points in analysing the data?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And are those individuals represented in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are part of the confidential annex D.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how did you identify the individuals in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through -- I don't understand. How did I identify --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are they identified by case name; are they identified by name; are they identified by ICMP ID number? That sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are identified by the name; first name, last name, and the father's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you have mentioned that you considered certain forensic evidence in terms of establishing what graves were associated with Srebrenica. And I may have neglected to ask you about this, but in respect of the Potocari graves, do you have any information concerning the bodies that have been testified to or there is evidence of that corroborate the account of DutchBat officers?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Potocari, we have two graves which were exhumed in 2006 and 2007, and those individuals were found -- 11 of those individuals is so far identified. So they are close to each other. Actually, one individual is in both graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me ask you, in respect of your involvement in determining the number of individuals associated with the Srebrenica and Zepa events, and based on your review of the forensic and DNA data, what do you reasonably expect in terms of the numbers you've established now and what they might -- what they might be in the future?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reasonably expect that the number will grow. So the total number, which is now in relation to the Srebrenica and Zepa victims is 6556 individuals so far identified. And I'm sure this number will grow. Since we don't have any identifications yet from the mass -- secondary mass graves of Cancari 1 and Cancari 2 which have already been exhumed and no individuals have yet been identified, and also since the work of the BiH authorities is ongoing, I expect that this number will for sure grow in the following years.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And let me just ask you one other question in the 30 seconds I have left. In respect of your DNA analysis, did you rely on information provided to you by the ICMP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And for the most recent report that you have generated, about when was that information received?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was received in February this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, and I would like to tender into evidence, it is 65 ter 6269, that is the ICMP information showing the matches to Srebrenica events. If you'd like me to show the witness part of it, I can do that as well, with your permission, since I'm out of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is this chart with -- it's not under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like for it to be under seal. It is all the -- all of the actual data that was provided for Mr. Janc's consideration, and it's essentially identical to the sample sheets that we went through earlier in his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And that concludes my direct examination. I appreciate your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 6269 will be Exhibit P213, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Janc, thank you for your patience. We have to adjourn now, but this is not the end of your examination. You will be recalled again for cross-examination by Mr. Tolimir. He indicated earlier that this will last for three hours. I'm not sure if that will be the right time, after the extensive examination-in-chief. The Chamber has to thank you for your attendance, and you are now free to go back to your normal activities. But bear in mind, please, no contact with the parties about the content of your evidence. Thank you very much again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the Court Officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I wanted to say that we will need at least six hours, at least, in view of this long examination lasting over two days by the Prosecutor. There are many things that are left unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it would be appreciated if you or your legal advisor would liaise with the Prosecution for the scheduling of the cross-examination and re-examination. Thank you very much for that. Before we adjourn, I would like to come back very shortly to the question of the numbering of intercept documents we discussed yesterday on page 1712 to 3 of the transcript of yesterday. The Chamber is of the view that the best way to proceed is as follows: The Registry will assign letters, suffixes, to different versions of the same intercept. We have received the original handwritten intercept as P162, and I think the best way to deal with this, because we have different originals with attached different translations, the best way to deal with this will be to have this already exhibited document as P162A, with attached translation. And the other, the transcript of this intercept, will then be P162B, with the attached relevant translation. This ruling refers only to intercept documents, because there are different originals, and so that they can be identified. Will the Registrar indicate that this will be received in that way.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 03142A is now Exhibit P162A. 65 ter 03142C is now Exhibit P162B. 65 ter 03142E is now Exhibit P162C. 65 ter 03142F is now Exhibit P162D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think there are no other procedural matters. I thank both parties for their very effective work, especially Mr. Vanderpuye. You see we are already on page 91. This is quite unusual. You made a good job. We adjourn, and we resume next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 17th day of May, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.53 p.m.,
